label: permits within transaction
type: the object statement or construct is legal inside the subject transaction scope, per a closed allow-list stated by the page.
note: The SQL++ transaction pages state statement legality as a closed list, not as prose - so this reads directly off the source. Batch B also minted conditionallyPermittedWithinTransaction (EXECUTE FUNCTION and PREPARE, whose legality depends on the UDF body rather than on the statement itself). Kept on the watchlist at recurrence 1 rather than promoted, but the finding behind it is real and worth recording: transaction-statement legality here is three-valued (permitted / conditional / prohibited), not binary, and the registry has no mechanism for qualifying a triple, so the conditional case currently has nowhere to live except a second predicate.
